message: In the twin under-deck Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) concept, the tuning basis has apparent 1.81 hertz versus 1.86 hertz conflict raised by Manager. To check it I used the vetted Den Hartog calculation (the Den Hartog optimum result (E3)). I found 1.81 hertz with 500 kilograms total mass and 64634 newtons per metre stiffness at 13.36 percent damper damping for 5.0 percent mass ratio, according to Den Hartog, 1934. I propose retaining 1.81 hertz as correct for this mass ratio, thank you Structural Dynamics Lead, since 1.86 hertz suits 2 percent ratio. My position: not ready because support safety remains open. In the same twin Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) concept, the added damping has verification need raised by Manager. To check it I used two-degree-of-freedom frequency response simulation (the two-degree-of-freedom response simulation (E6)). I found 9.44 percent effective damping rising from 0.4 percent inherent damping, according to Den Hartog, 1947. I propose retaining two 250 kilogram units on coil springs with viscous dampers hung below girders. My position: not ready because comfort acceptance is still undecided. In the 40 metre footbridge retrofit concept, the vertical crowd acceleration has uncomfortable peaks. To check it I used the same response simulation (the two-degree-of-freedom response simulation (E6)) with the maintained under-deck layout (the under-deck twin-unit layout sketch (E7)). I found reduction from 17.50 metres per second squared to 0.74 metres per second squared with 20.0 millimetres travel, reaching Comfort Level (CL) CL2 below 1.0 metre per second squared, according to Setra, 2006.
